title: Randomized Controlled Trial to Assess the Effect of a Multimodal Virtual Reality-Supported Therapy on the Quality of Life of Patients During Inpatient Treatment with Intensive Chemotherapy and Stem Cell Transplantation (VR-SUPPORT)
summary:
Patients after high-dose chemotherapy and/or stem cell transplantation have a long inpatient stay, during which they often severely degrade both physically, mentally and cognitively, which leads to a significant reduction in quality of life. Physiotherapy can only spend little time per patient due to the limited staff capacity, cognitive exercises are not provided for in everyday clinical life.

This study is intended to investigate whether the use of VR-assisted exercise and occupational therapy in these patients leads to an improvement in the quality of life during and after inpatient treatment. After fulfilling inclusion and exclusion criteria, randomization takes place into a control group and an intervention group. The intervention group receives VR glasses with suitable motion- and concentration-promoting applications for free independent use.

At three times during the stay as well as at one time after discharge, tests are carried out to record physical and mental performance and quality of life. Finally, the results are compared with those of the control group with the question of whether the quality of life is improved by the intervention.

interventions.name: Intervention group (receives a VR headset with suitable applications promoting movement and concentration for free independent use during standard care).
Control group (receives only standard care without the use of VR headsets).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Written consent after clarification

- Ability to follow instructions in German or English

- Inpatient treatment for one of the following therapies:

High-dose chemotherapy for acute leukemia or autologous or allogeneic stem cell transplantation
Exclusion criteria:
- Serious cardiac diseases (e.g. heart failure NYHA III, myocardial infarction <3 months)

- Severe infection or sepsis CTCAE v5 > III

- Severe global pulmonary insufficiency

- Severe neurological, amnestic or cognitive impairments

- Lack of technical skills
